preflight.note: Opened from direct operator feedback after native Workbench validation: collection-heavy sidebar pages require excessive vertical scrolling. The operator specifically requested Work tabs Proposed, Active, Deferred, Complete and the same user-centric low-scroll pattern across all sidebar pages.

acceptance_criteria.text: Introduce one reusable accessible secondary-tab primitive used across sidebar pages, with count support, clear selected state, correct tablist/tab/panel ARIA relationships, keyboard Left/Right/Home/End navigation, focus-visible behavior, and responsive wrapping without page-wide horizontal scrolling.

Work presents exactly four primary lifecycle tabs in this order: Proposed, Active, Deferred, Complete; Active contains blocked records in a clearly labelled Blocked group before ordinary active/in-progress records while retaining each blocked record's canonical blocked status.

Work tab counts, selected-item behavior, search scoping, refresh/transition reconciliation, and useful default selection are deterministic; Active count includes active plus blocked, and a moved item cannot remain misleadingly selected under the wrong lifecycle tab.

Add reusable bounded client-side pagination for collection-heavy views with a shared practical page size, Previous/Next controls, disabled boundaries, start-end-of-total range text, deterministic ordering, and safe reset/clamping after search/tab/snapshot changes; Complete must not render the full completed corpus as one long page.
Dashboard uses concise Overview, Attention, and Session secondary views; Attention surfaces actionable validation/blocked-work signals with navigation rather than duplicating long source lists.

Decisions uses Current, Proposed, Deferred, and History tabs with accepted -> Current, proposed -> Proposed, deferred -> Deferred, and rejected/superseded/deprecated -> History; counts and deterministic newest-first ordering use snapshot-derived typed metadata rather than N+1 detail reads.

Evidence uses Recent, Passed, Attention, and All tabs; Recent is newest-first and bounded, Passed contains passed runs, Attention contains failed/partial/blocked runs, All is paged, and summary rows surface useful result/time/work-item metadata without per-record detail fetches.
Graph uses Dependencies, Evidence, Governance, and All tabs derived from existing typed edge kinds while retaining the accessible table representation and bounded local paging.
Validation uses Errors, Warnings, Info, and All tabs with counts and highest-severity non-empty default behavior, while preserving a compact all-clear state when no diagnostics exist.
Analysis uses Constraints, Suggestions, and Facts tabs mapped exactly from the existing finding classification values and preserves remediation/explanatory content.

Settings uses Appearance, Session, and Boundaries tabs; presentation/theme controls are discoverable under Appearance while session/watcher identity and native/security boundary explanations remain distinct.

Any richer Decision/Evidence list metadata is exposed through typed Rust desktop summary DTOs (or an equivalently typed snapshot projection), generated into TypeScript, and derived from the current cached RepositorySnapshot/index without opening every record, building fresh snapshots, or adding Git queries.

Secondary-tab, search, sort, and page changes are presentation-only operations over the cached native generation: executable tests prove they cause zero new repository snapshots, zero Git subprocesses, and no N+1 desktop API detail calls for unchanged data.

Existing Work detail inspection, Decision/Evidence detail panes, Rust-owned create/edit/transition mutation planning, stale-plan handling, watcher refresh, and repository-switch behavior remain intact and accessible after the information-architecture refactor.

Frontend and desktop tests cover tab mappings/counts, blocked-under-Active behavior, paging/search interaction, keyboard/ARIA semantics, per-sidebar-page sub-tab memory, repository-switch reset, Decisions/Evidence no-N+1 behavior, Graph/Validation/Analysis grouping, and WI057 process/cache non-regression.

Native Windows Workbench acceptance confirms the requested Work tab layout, bounded Complete browsing, coherent user-centric secondary tabs across every sidebar section, usable narrow-window behavior, materially reduced scrolling, normal detail/mutation navigation, and no terminal/process-amplification regression; closeout evidence records all relevant regression counts and WI056 compatibility status.
